g.text: 1. Printed body 60 x 60 x 14 mm. The nest is the union of the puck outline (+0.25) at 0° and turned 180° about the nest centre: it accepts the marker
in exactly these two positions; its centre moves 4.6 mm between them (deviation D15).
2. Seat for the stainless reference plate at z = -1.6; the three ball feet rest on the plate top (z = -0.1). Bond the plate with a thin
epoxy film on three pads only, then check flatness - the plate, not the print, is the tilt reference.
3. Cradle PCB top at z = -4.69 so that each spring pin is at its recommended working height (5.82) on a pad 1.13 above the puck base plane.
4. OPEN (D17): the seven pins push the 11 g marker up with about 4 N. No hold-down is modelled; one is required before the cradle can
charge reliably or serve as the flip-calibration seat. At 180° the pins bear on the solid base plate (no pad, no opening).
5. Pin and receptacle envelopes are PROVISIONAL. Sheet 2: reference plate, pin row section, 0° / 180° positions.
